title: Counting & cyclic sort
learn: counting/bucket sort for small ranges; cyclic sort pattern: numbers 1..n → put each at index n-1
hook: Missing Number, Find All Disappeared Numbers and First Missing Positive all hide the same trick: when values are 1..n, a value can point to its own index. That gives O(n) time with O(1) space, which is exactly what the follow-up asks for.

explain.prompt: Explain cyclic sort and how it finds missing numbers in an array containing values from 1 to n, in O(n) time and O(1) space.
keyPoints: value v belongs at index v − 1
swap each value to its home until the current slot holds the right value or a duplicate
each swap puts one value home for good → at most n swaps, O(n) time, O(1) space
afterwards any index i not holding i + 1 reveals a missing number (and the value there is a duplicate)
